statement: Domaine Huet states that Victor Huet and his son Gaston founded the domaine in Vouvray in 1928.
Domaine Huet currently describes thirty hectares of Chenin Blanc across three named sites: Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont and Clos du Bourg.

scope_notes: This records the producer's stated encounter/adoption chronology; it does not invent a certification date.
statement: Domaine Huet says its encounter with biodynamic farming began in 1988 and describes biodynamic farming as its continuing estate practice.
Domaine Huet describes Le Haut-Lieu as a fifteen-hectare plateau site with very deep brown-clay soil.

scope_notes: No residual-sugar threshold is encoded here; the current 2023 specification is linked from INAO and a 2026 modification process is pending.
statement: INAO describes Vouvray as an AOP for Chenin Blanc on the right bank of the Loire producing dry, demi-sec, moelleux and sparkling wines.

scope_notes: A persistent wine identity across vintages does not mean the wine is non-vintage; vintage-specific facts belong on dated claims.
statement: Domaine Huet Le Haut-Lieu Sec is a recurring vintage-dated Vouvray wine identity associated with the Le Haut-Lieu site and Chenin Blanc; CARTA represents it as one durable wine entity across vintages.
Domaine Huet is based in Vouvray, and Le Haut-Lieu is a named Huet vineyard within the Vouvray wine context.
Arnot-Roberts says Duncan Arnot Meyers and Nathan Lee Roberts founded the winery in Healdsburg in 2001.
Arnot-Roberts identifies Clary Ranch Syrah as a wine from Clary Ranch in the Petaluma Gap.
Arnot-Roberts says Paul Clary planted Pinot Noir and Syrah at Clary Ranch in 2000.
Arnot-Roberts currently describes Clary Ranch as owned and tended by Drew Beuchley and the same crew that has worked the vines since planting.

scope_notes: No coordinates or parcel polygon are inferred.
statement: Arnot-Roberts places Clary Ranch in the heart of the Petaluma Gap near Tomales Bay and gives the vineyard elevation as 300 feet.

scope_notes: Producer-described current site practice; CARTA does not generalize this to every Arnot-Roberts source vineyard.
statement: Arnot-Roberts lists Clary Ranch as organically farmed and says the protracted growing season and clay-loam soils allow farming without irrigation.
Arnot-Roberts lists Clary Ranch as clone/selection 470 on Steinbeck-series sedimentary clay-loam soils.
TTB established the Petaluma Gap American Viticultural Area in 2017, with the rule effective in January 2018.
Arnot-Roberts says Caitlin Quinn joined the winery as assistant winemaker in 2015, with Syrah central to her stated interest in the project.
Louis Michel & Fils presents the domaine as a Chablis family estate making wine since 1850.
Louis Michel & Fils states that it vinifies exclusively in stainless steel; its Vaudésir is matured for 18 to 20 months only in stainless-steel tanks.
Louis Michel & Fils bottles Chablis Grand Cru Vaudésir from its parcel in the Vaudésir climat as a Chardonnay wine within its Grand Cru range.

scope_notes: This describes the domaine's parcel, not the whole Vaudésir climat.
statement: Louis Michel & Fils describes its Vaudésir parcel as north-facing and Kimmeridgian, with white clay and limestone plus chalk on steeper parts and browner clay toward the west.
Louis Michel & Fils lists planting years of 1950, 1960 and 1970 for its Vaudésir parcel.

scope_notes: Current producer-described protocol for this wine; not a Chablis Grand Cru legal requirement.
statement: Louis Michel & Fils describes Vaudésir fermentation with indigenous yeasts in temperature-controlled tanks, spontaneous malolactic fermentation, 18 to 20 months in stainless steel, bentonite fining if needed and one light filtration before bottling.
Vaudésir is one of the seven named climats within the Chablis Grand Cru AOP; CARTA therefore keeps Vaudésir as a climat/vineyard identity rather than inventing a separate appellation entity for it.
The Chablis wine board describes the approximately 15.4-hectare Vaudésir climat as a natural amphitheater with contrasting exposures, significant clay and Kimmeridgian marly limestone.
Louis Michel & Fils is based in Chablis, and the Chablis Grand Cru vineyards lie on the right bank of the Serein in the Chablis commune.
The Brunello di Montalcino Consorzio states that Caparzo was established in 1970.

scope_notes: CARTA records the separately vinified vineyard wine as an early/first Consorzio-described cru concept without inflating it to a broader unsupported 'first single-vineyard wine in Italy' claim.
statement: The Consorzio says Caparzo introduced the cru concept to Montalcino in 1977 by vinifying La Casa separately; Caparzo identifies 1977 as the first vintage of Brunello di Montalcino Vigna La Casa.
The Consorzio states that Elisabetta Gnudi Angelini purchased Caparzo in 1998.

scope_notes: First-party figures correct the conflicting 220–250 m and 500–550 m elevations in the Run 03E research report.
statement: Caparzo describes La Casa as five hectares of Brunello vines at 275 metres, with south-to-southeast exposure on schist-clay soil known as galestro.

scope_notes: The first-party site connects the La Casa farm and surrounding Vigna La Casa vineyards to Montosoli; CARTA preserves the hill relationship provisionally without inventing a Montosoli polygon or exact slope position.
statement: Caparzo places the La Casa property and its surrounding Brunello di Montalcino Vigna La Casa vineyard context on the Montosoli hill near Montalcino.

scope_notes: Current producer-described protocol; not treated as universal across historical vintages.
statement: Caparzo currently describes Vigna La Casa as spending its first 12 months in French oak barriques followed by 24 months in 30-hectolitre French oak barrels.

scope_notes: This corrects Run 03E's claim that Brunello law requires 36 months in oak.
statement: The current Consorzio production-rules page states that Brunello di Montalcino is made from Sangiovese, requires a minimum of two years in oak and four months in bottle, and is confined to the historical borders of the municipality of Montalcino.
The Brunello di Montalcino Consorzio states that Sangiovese is also called Brunello in Montalcino.
Caparzo identifies Massimo Bracalente as its winemaker/oenologist in current producer material.
Caparzo and its La Casa vineyard are in the municipality of Montalcino within the Brunello di Montalcino production area.
